html:
The Irritila were a Native American people of the Laguna region, around the old lakes of Coahuila and Durango in northern Mexico. Spanish writers often called them Laguneros, "lake people".

They lived by fishing, hunting water birds and gathering plants along the lakes and the Nazas River, a richer life than most desert peoples had. Jesuits founded a mission among them at Parras in 1598. Epidemics and Spanish ranching broke them up, and by about 1700 they no longer appear in records. See also Irritilas on the modern map.
